nomenclature.etymology_html:
- Digitaria: From the Latin digitus- finger, alluding to the radiating inflorescence.
- ciliaris: From the Latin cilium-eyelids, in reference to the ciliated nerves or margin of the glumes or lemmas.

seed.text: The fruit of Digitaria ciliaris is a caryopis. The grain is ellipsoid in shape, it is grey to light brown in colour.

flower.text: The inflorescences of Digitaria ciliaris are digitate or subdigitate. The axis of the inflorescence can be up to 5 cm long in robust specimens. They are composed of 2 to 12 stiff racemes. Each raceme is 6 to 22 cm long. The racemes are sometimes adorned with sparse long white hairs. There are 3 anthers.
flower.text_html:
The inflorescences of Digitaria ciliaris are digitate or subdigitate. 
The axis of the inflorescence can be up to 5 cm long in robust specimens. 
They are composed of 2 to 12 stiff racemes. Each raceme is 6 to 22 cm long. 
The racemes are sometimes adorned with sparse long white hairs. 
There are 3 anthers.

leaf.text: The leaves of Digitaria ciliaris are linear to linear-lanceolate in shape. They are 5 to 20 cm long and 0.3 to 1 cm wide. The adaxial surface of the leaves are usually pilose. The leaf margins are thickened and scabrous. The ligule is less than 2 mm long and has an eciliate membrane.
leaf.text_html:
The leaves of Digitaria ciliaris are linear to linear-lanceolate in shape. 
They are 5 to 20 cm long and 0.3 to 1 cm wide. 
The adaxial surface of the leaves are usually pilose. 
The leaf margins are thickened and scabrous. 
The ligule is less than 2 mm long and has an eciliate membrane.

habit.text: Digitaria ciliaris is a annual herb with erect culms growing up to 1 m tall. The grass is sometimes decumbent, rarely creeping and rooting at the lower nodes.

stem_bark.text: The culms of Digitaria ciliaris are growing from 20 cm to 1 m tall. They are decumbent at the base and geniculately ascending.
